messages.subject: Extracting summaries using runModels
parts:
Hi there,

I'm trying to compare model summaries that I've run using the runModels command in MplusAutomation. The output of my models are in a directory folder "/Documents/Projects/LCA_comparison"

When I type:

sum <- readModels("/Documents/Projects/LCA_comparison", what="summaries")$summaries
sum

I get "NULL"

Is it possible to get summary statistics from a bunch of models within a folder this way? Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks!

messages.author: 3945e838ed92472f
messages.subject: Re: Extracting summaries using runModels
parts:
Hi Melissa, 
For model summaries I use extractModelSummaries. This is on windows but I imagine would be applicable to mac. Hope this helps, 

Nick 


mySummaries1 <- extractModelSummaries("C:/aim1", recursive=TRUE)
write.table(mySummaries1,paste('model summaries','.csv',sep=""),row.names=FALSE, col.names=TRUE, quote=F, sep=',')

messages.author: 3945e838ed92472f
messages.subject: Re: Extracting summaries using runModels
parts:
I didn't know that it had been deprecated...

Using readModels and the loop function Michael just helped me with, this appears to create the model fit summary. 



mySummaries <-readModels("C:/aim 1", what="summaries", recursive=TRUE)

combined_sum <- do.call(dplyr::bind_rows, lapply(1:length(mySummaries), function(m) { 
      df <- mySummaries[[m]]$summaries
      return(df)
    }))


write.table(combined_sum,paste('model fit summaries','.csv',sep=""),row.names=FALSE, col.names=TRUE, quote=F, sep=',')
